tldr: Agent Laboratory is an autonomous LLM-based framework that completes the entire ML research pipeline—from literature review through experimentation to report writing—and significantly reduces research costs while producing competitive results, especially when humans provide feedback at each stage.
contributions: Introduction of Agent Laboratory, an open-source LLM agent framework for accelerating individual ML research
Human evaluation showing o1-preview perceived as most useful and o1-mini achieved highest experimental quality scores
Demonstration of a gap between automated and human evaluations, with automated scores significantly overestimating quality (6.1/10 vs 3.8/10)
Co-pilot mode evaluated showing higher overall scores than autonomous mode
Cost analysis showing only $2.33 USD per paper with gpt-4o backend and an 84% cost reduction compared to prior autonomous research methods
methods: Agent Laboratory accepts a human-provided research idea and progresses through three stages: literature review (using arXiv API to curate papers), experimentation (with PhD/Postdoc agents formulating plans, ML Engineer agents preparing data and running experiments via mle-solver, and iterative self-reflection), and report writing (using paper-solver to generate and iteratively refine a NeurIPS-style paper). The framework supports both fully autonomous mode and co-pilot mode, where humans review outputs at checkpoints between phases and can request revisions. Evaluations were conducted across five topics with human surveys and automated NeurIPS-style peer review.
results: Agent Laboratory driven by o1-preview generates the best research outcomes. Generated ML code achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods. Human involvement via co-pilot feedback at each stage significantly improves overall research quality. Co-pilot mode achieved higher overall scores than autonomous mode. Agent Laboratory achieves an 84% decrease in research expenses compared to previous autonomous research methods, costing only $2.33 USD per paper with a gpt-4o backend. Automated evaluations significantly overestimated quality (6.1/10 vs 3.8/10 overall), with similar discrepancies in clarity and contribution metrics.
limitations: LLMs exhibit weaknesses in feasibility and implementation details of research ideation. There is a significant gap between automated and human evaluations, with automated scores overestimating quality. Co-pilot mode involves trade-offs in experimental quality and usefulness, reflecting challenges in aligning agent outputs with researcher intent. Self-reported ethical concerns were marked as false across evaluated papers, but the system's reliance on LLM-based automated reviewing may produce unreliable assessments.
